text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government says it is premature to reach conclusions on whether progress has been achieved or not in the United Nations proximity talks between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides.
- Cyprus may report Turkey to the international aviation body Eurocontrol for its failure to allow Cyprus Airways planes to fly in Turkish airspace on flights to Moscow and Helsinki.
- United Nations envoy Gustave Feissel confirms Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash is to meet U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan next week.
- British U.N. officer escapes court martial in indecent assault case.
- Family from Erimi village in Limassol claim a cabinet member is involved in disputed transfer of several hectares of land from them to his own company.
- The government is cutting benefits to the handicapped.
- No progress has been achieved on the essence of the Cyprus problem after three weeks of proximity talks. The Turkish side violates Cyprus's airspace and seeks indirect recognition.
- Hospitals come to a standstill. Doctors declare a 48 hour strike.
- Rauf Denktash seeks recognition of his pseudo-state by the adoption of measures to improve the climate for talks.
